data.text: Under credit agreement §9.08, the maximum net leverage ratio must be at most 5.00x, and the company fails this with 5.12x in this scenario. Under credit agreement §9.07, the minimum interest coverage ratio must be at least 3.00x, and the company fails this with 1.47x.

An earnings decline of 30% drops EBITDA to $641M and produces a negative free cash flow per year of -$99M. Refinancing debt at 10.00% pushes annual interest to $436M, resulting in an interest coverage of 1.47x. Net leverage hits 5.12x, breaching the 5.00x cap.

Lend. Sure, the net leverage hits 5.12x against the 5.00x cap and interest coverage drops to 1.47x, but look at the liquidity cushion with $1.48B in the undrawn revolver and $1.08B of cash. We can easily secure a waiver with tighter terms while they ride out this temporary dip.

Don't lend. Both loan covenants are breached with net leverage hitting 5.12x against the 5.00x cap and interest coverage collapsing to 1.47x. The limit tightens further to 4.50x in 2028, exactly when $1.38B of debt comes due.
